units.en: The effect is initially rather weak, as it only provides a 5% bonus. This means that (land) equipment with 80% reliability will get boosted to 84% (80 × 1.05). However, this bonus increases by an additional 5% per level (for 10%, 15%, and 20%, respectively). This allows reliability improvements to equipment that normally cannot be upgraded. Mechanized are the most significant, but also motorized, all of the towed weapons, and support equipment. It benefits infantry equipment too, but infantry equipment is easy to produce and starts at 90% reliability, rather than the usual 80%. Waiting until Maintenance Company II before considering using it isn't a bad idea.

For equipment that can be upgraded, such as aircraft, it means putting upgrade points into reliability is less necessary, unless it drops below 80% (or let it drop lower and focus on maintaining 80% reliability after the bonus). That can potentially save a lot of XP. With ⟦0⟧, vehicle designs with low reliability, such as using petrol-electric engines, become more feasible. Of course, that would require all divisions using tanks of that design to have a maintenance company.
No Step Back
As of 1.5, Maintenance companies can also capture equipment from enemy divisions (equal to their reliability boost) that would otherwise be destroyed.

Armored Maintenance Company is a variant of the maintenance company made available after completing the 1938 technology of the same name that requires having completed the Military Engineering Vehicles special project. It uses armored support vehicle equipment in place of some support equipment and infantry equipment. The equipment differences mean it has increased production cost and adds fuel usage to any division it is added to, but it also provides some additional Armor, Piercing, Soft Attack, Hard Attack, Defense, and Breakthrough to the division depending on the equipment variant(s) used. Compared to maintenance companies, they also provide additional HP to armor battalions and add equipment recovery to attached divisions. Upgrades to armored maintenance companies provide lower reliability bonuses compared to upgrades to maintenance companies, but increased equipment capture ratios and equipment recovery rates, making them more useful in tank divisions, especially compared to regular maintenance companies.
Field Hospital (HOS)

These provide three bonuses. First, with the 1936 hospital, 20% of the losses in combat get returned to the manpower pool rather than being lost forever, also removing the impact of those losses on War Support. Second, 10% less XP is lost from combat losses. Third, all infantry, motorized, and mechanized battalions provide 10% more HP, leading to fewer equipment losses from battle, especially on the attack. Upgrading field hospitals increases the first two of these bonuses. The more combat a division sees over time, the greater the overall benefit from a field hospital, especially when attacking in poorly supplied conditions. Conversely, they are a waste in a division unlikely to see sustained combat or likely to be eliminated if engaged in combat, such as some security, garrison, or coastal defense divisions.

Helicopter Med-Evac is a variant of the field hospital company made available after completing the 1938 Helicopter Med-Evac Company technology that requires having completed the Helicopters special project. It requires helicopter equipment in place of some truck equipment. The equipment differences mean it has increased production cost and adds fuel usage to any division it is added to, but it also provides some additional Armor, Piercing, Defense, and Breakthrough to the division. Compared to field hospitals, helicopter med-evacs have greater supply use and provide less XP loss reduction and bonus HP, but they provide greater manpower trickleback and war support protection and provide additional Recovery Rate to all infantry, motorized, and mechanized battalions. Upgrading helicoptier med-evacs provides smaller bonuses to XP loss reduction compared to upgrading field hospitals, but instead provices greater bonuses to manpower trickleback, war support protection, and bonus Recovery Rate.

From the manpower, war support, and HP perspectives, bigger is better. Each field hospital, being percentage-based, will simply save more lives and equipment in a large division than in a small one. This applies doubly so for helicopter med-evacs, as their bonus recovery rate is also percentage-based, and their fuel usage relative to the entire division goes down as the number of fuel-using battalions in the division increases.

From an XP perspective, however, each soldier is worth more XP in a smaller division. So, it can be worth adding them to a small number of elite divisions. These could be things like marine or paratroop divisions, etc. Another possibility might be a regular infantry division that has already gained a high experience level on its own. By creating a duplicate template, a field hospital can be added to some divisions but not to otherwise identical ones, to help those high XP divisions keep their XP. The higher a division's XP gets, the more the average will be reduced by casualties (since replacements are always green). Deploying new divisions that have a field hospital while they are still green is a complete waste from the XP perspective. Therefore, you have more incentive to train new divisions up to regular before deployment when using field hospitals.
Logistics (LOG)

These provide a flat 10% reduction in supply consumption and a 5% reduction in fuel usage, which improves with upgrades. Since it's percentage based, they will provide the most benefit in the most supply-hungry divisions. Since artillery uses a lot of supplies, divisions with multiple artillery of any type (line/support/self-propelled) are the first place to look. Just open the division designer and compare the Supply Use stat before and after adding the company, then decide if it's worth it. Most large divisions are potential candidates. For infantry, keep in mind that when fighting in places with high infrastructure, where months of fighting can go by without units running low on supply, a logistics company provides no benefit. Creating a separate infantry division template specifically for low-supply areas is an option. Other divisions can use that support slot for more combat-related purposes.

Helicopter Transports are a variant of the logistics company made available after completing the 1938 Helicopter Transport Company technology that requires having completed the Helicopters special project. It requires additional helicopter equipment in addition to the normal equipment required by a logistics company. This means it has increased production cost, but it also provides some additional Armor, Piercing, Defense, and Breakthrough to the division. Unlike other helicopter support company variants, it does not add fuel usage to a division that does not have any to begin with, but it does increase fuel usage percentage-wise for any division that already has it instead of decreasing it the way a regular logistics company would. Otherwise, compared to a logistics company, helicopter transports provide additional movement speed in most terrain types. Upgrading helicopter tranports also provides bigger supply usage reductions compared to upgrading logistics companies, though their percentage-wise increase to fuel usage remains. As their only downsides compared to logistics companies come from them increasing fuel usage instead of decreasing it, they are straight upgrades to regular logistics companies for divisions that would not otherwise use fuel, such as infantry or special forces divisions without any armored or motorized support companies.
Signal (SIG)

Signal companies provide the Initiative stat, which speeds up joining combat in progress from reserves, as well as planning speed. In general these are most useful for troops in frequent front-line combat, or for reserves in critical positions where rapid reinforcement is needed. Used in the right place, these can be great.

One example is if a division at the top of the reserves has a Signal Company, the division will be more likely to fill the hole in the front line faster. Without a Signal Company, the base chance to reinforce a battle (assuming that there is available width in the battlefield) is 2% every hour. This means there is a 50% chance that a division will have reinforced the battle within 35 hours. If the Radio technology has been researched, this increases to 4% chance to reinforce every hour, and there is then a 50% chance that the division will have reinforced the battle within 17 hours. The 1936 Signal Company increase Initiative by 10%, and every following upgrade adds 12% Initiative. Each 1% extra Initiative increases reinforce rate by 0.25%, meaning that 10% Initiative adds 2.5% to the reinforcement chance - thus, there is a 6.5% chance for the division to reinforce every hour. So a division with a 1936 Signal Company will have a 50% chance to reinforce a battle within 11 hours.

Planning speed is increased by 1% for every 1% of a division's Initiative. Given that the base planning speed is 2% per day, a 1936 Signal Company will add an additional 0.2% planning bonus per day, and thus save 3 days to reach the standard 50 % bonus (II:4 days; III: 6 days; IV: 7 days). Whether bonus Initiative expedites preparation of invasions or paradrops is unconfirmed.

Armored Signal Company is a variant of the signal company made available after completing the 1938 technology of the same name that requires having completed the Military Engineering Vehicles special project. It uses armored support vehicle equipment in place of some support equipment and truck equipment. The equipment differences mean it has increased production cost and adds fuel usage to any division it is added to, but it can also provides some additional Armor, Piercing, Soft Attack, Hard Attack, Defense, and Breakthrough to the division depending on the equipment variant(s) used. Compared to a signal company, it also provides additional Breakthrough to armor battalions. Without any upgrades, it gives more Initiative than a regular signal company, but from the 1939 signal company upgrade onwards, it provides less Initiative than a regular signal company. Upgrades to armored signal companies do increase the bonus Initiative they give (albeit at a much lower rate than for regular signal companies), and they also increase the additional Breakthrough they provide to armor battalions. Because dedicated tank-heavy divisions tend to have fairly high Breakthrough already and the main benefit of using armored or regular signal companies would be the bonus Initiative where armored signal companies provide an inferior bonus, armored signal companies are only better than regular signal companies in under niche circumstances, probably involving an offensive division that has just a few tank battalions that could benefit from the additional Breakthrough more.
Helicopter Brigade (HEL)

⟦0⟧ introduced the Helicopter Brigade support company, which is unlocked by completing the Helicopters special project. Where other helicopter support companies like helicopter recon, helicopter med-evac, and helicopter tranports are specialized alternatives to non-helicopter-based support companies, the helicopter brigade functions as something standalone that can be added to a division regardless of what other support companies it is using. On top of the extra Armor, Piercing, Defense, and Breakthrough that the company provides from its use of helicopter equipment, the helicopter brigade provides a mix of bonuses that the other three, more specialized companies would give: extra Reconnaissance, reduced Supply Use, extra manpower trickleback, extra war support protection, reduced XP loss from taking losses, and extra HP for infantry, motorized, and mechanized battalions. These bonuses, however, are only upgraded by the 1942 technology upgrades for recon companies, logistics companies, and field hospitals, which can make fully upgrading helicopter brigades more difficult compared to one of the specialized helicopter support companies. Unlike the more specialized companies though, helicopter brigades neither add fuel usage nor increase existing fuel usage.

Because of their diluted bonuses spread across so many things, helicopter brigades are most effective when they are paired up with one or two dedicated support companies for its roles while also acting as a minor replacement for a different dedicated support company. For example, if a division would previously have had both a logistics company and a field hospital and the player has decided to use it in a theater where supply usage is a huge concern but still wants to minimize manpower losses, it can be beneficial to swap out the field hospital for a helicopter brigade to get that extra bit of supply usage reduction without completely losing all of the field hospital's bonuses.
